note: Why a personality decision did not run, or ran without personality turning it, in the trait-wiring audit (docs/reports/trait-wiring-2026-10-20.md). One row per decision with a gap; the matrix (scripts/traits/trait-wiring-matrix.ts) joins them. A row is removed when its fix lands.

corruption.offer.why: Runs when a lobbyist meets a member on a bill with employer costs (src/core2/modules/interest-groups.ts). Honesty now weighs it person by person: in South Windham, Connecticut's year 190 of 1,142 offers the money alone would have made were withheld for the lobbyist's honesty, and in Langley, Washington's 5 of 1,082; no offer was made in either, so taking and the chain behind it did not run.
corruption.offer.fix: Calibrate the offer's honest pull to the asks play makes, so some offers are made (people-corruption-honest-pull-calibrated).

corruption.take.why: Runs after an offer says yes (src/core2/modules/corruption.ts, considerBribe): once in Jerry City, Ohio's played year (taken) and 1,156 times in New Britain, Connecticut's, where the third leaning most toward taking took 0.5 percent and the least none. Too few takes in either year show the study's odds (Pletzer et al. 2019, honesty-humility rho -0.48).
corruption.take.fix: Calibrate the offer side so offers vary by person (people-corruption-honest-pull-calibrated).

corruption.tell.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
corruption.tell.why: Needs a taken bribe's crime row (src/core2/modules/corruption.ts:215); none was written.

justice.report.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
justice.report.why: Needs a crime row from corruption (src/core2/modules/justice.ts:250); ran twice from other crimes.

justice.prosecute.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes

justice.plea.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes

press.tip.class: trigger needs a record nobody writes
press.tip.why: Needs a crime.told event for a taken bribe (src/core2/modules/press.ts:2049).

recalls.organize.why: A petition starts from a county or city ordinance where the state allows recall without grounds (src/core2/modules/recalls.ts, weighOrdinance), or, where it requires grounds, from a charge or a press exposure of a serving local official that the town heard of (noteMisconduct, weighMisconduct). Neither South Windham, Connecticut nor Langley, Washington held either in its year; with a fixture charge in Sylvan Grove, Kansas, the printed story reached 71 of 76 named residents and a petition started two weeks later (src/core2/recall-for-cause.test.ts).
recalls.organize.fix: Charges come from the bribe chain once offers are made (people-corruption-honest-pull-calibrated).

recalls.sign.why: Follows an organizer (src/core2/modules/recalls.ts, startRecall); see recalls.organize.

recalls.vote.why: Needs a petition that reached the ballot (src/core2/modules/recalls.ts, recallWork); see recalls.organize.

ballot-measures.vote.class: runs only on a date outside the year
ballot-measures.vote.why: The earliest measure in data/elections/ballot-measures.json is June 16, 2026; the played year ends January 20, 2026.
ballot-measures.vote.fix: Add odd-year measures or let an ordinance refer a local measure.

voting.turnout.class: runs only on a date outside the year
voting.turnout.why: The played year runs January 20, 2025 to January 20, 2026; most places hold no election in 2025, so turnout runs only where a 2025 local or state election exists.
voting.turnout.fix: Seed odd-year local elections where the place holds them; measure in a second year otherwise.

voting.back-incumbent.class: runs only on a date outside the year

voting.exit-poll.class: runs only on a date outside the year

campaigns.answer-poll.why: Needs a campaign that has set aside enough for a poll (src/core2/modules/campaigns.ts, pollFund against pollMinimumInterviews); no local campaign in four played places did.
campaigns.answer-poll.fix: Weight calibrated from the adults of a drawn town (campaigns.traits.test.ts); the call-time path runs when a state or federal campaign raises enough.

offices.accept-appointment.why: Runs only when a serving local official dies or moves away and the post fills by appointment (src/core2/modules/offices.ts:1067).
offices.accept-appointment.fix: Add resignation as a vacancy cause.

constituent-cases.handle-case.why: The official's own call now comes first, and their staffer carries it out (src/core2/modules/constituent-cases.ts, officeHandles). It ran 17 times in Jerry City, Ohio's played year and 438 times in New Britain, Connecticut's, and every official helped: the case is the same constant every time (constituentHelpBase), so a weight only sets a trait bar and cannot reach the study's odds (Barrick and Mount 1991, conscientiousness r .22, 2.44 between the thirds). The general weight of 1 stands.
constituent-cases.handle-case.fix: Give the case its own circumstances (the problem's severity, the office's open cases), then calibrate (traits-integrity-cases-vary).

conversation.believe-claim.why: Read only when the player's line makes a claim (src/director/conversation.ts:2169).
conversation.believe-claim.fix: Read it where people pass on claims to each other (speech retell, news pass-on).

conversation.reply-reach.why: Read only in a conversation the player opens.
conversation.reply-reach.fix: Player-only by design; covered by the player's conversations.

bring-it-up.blame.why: Read only in a conversation the player opens (src/director/bring-it-up.ts:105).

press.dig.class: runs only on a date outside the year
press.dig.why: Follows an interview answer that contradicts a record (src/core2/modules/press.ts:1753).

estates.will.why: Runs when someone with an estate dies (src/core2/estates.ts:283).

office-day-state.clemency.why: A weekly clemency petition for a governor who is not the player is in review on another branch.

housing.buy-home.why: Runs at the housing review but every household keeps renting (the buy baseline and down-payment terms outweigh any lean).
housing.buy-home.fix: Calibrate the buy reasons so some households buy, then the trait weight.

jobs.apply.why: Ran 545 times; the pick never changed with personality.

jobs.review-worker.why: Ran 2,059 times; the pick never changed with personality.

drives.respond.why: Personality turned none of 1,471 drive responses in Ely, Nevada at any weight up to 8: the drive's own strength separates the options. No study gives a size (neuroticism and rumination is the direction).
drives.respond.fix: None until the options score closer or a study gives a size; the general trait weight of 1 stands.

school.attend.why: Children attend 99.95% of school days (10,587 kept weighings, Ely, Nevada); personality turns none below a weight of 1 and at 1 the third least inclined misses at 11 times the odds. Real chronic absence is far higher and follows illness, family and poverty, which the school choice does not read (src/core2/modules/school.ts:149). Poropat 2009 (conscientiousness r 0.19) measures performance, not attendance.
school.attend.fix: Give the school choice the child's illness and the household's circumstances, then calibrate.

life.daily-act.why: Personality turned 14.8% of 29,520 daily-activity picks at the general trait weight of 1. Studies of extraversion and time spent socializing (Mehl et al. 2006) report no extractable coefficient, so the general weight stands.
life.daily-act.fix: Calibrate when a study gives a size for extraversion and social time.

campaigns.volunteer.why: Most adults a campaign reaches share one reason total: no warmth toward the candidate yet, no tie, no family link and no work hours (src/core2/modules/campaigns.ts volunteerReason). Where the yes line falls inside that pile, temperament alone sorts them, so one town's odds ratio between the thirds of lean runs from about 1 to over 30 (Red Cliff, Colorado, 424 calls: 34.6 at a one-in-twenty yes share, against Mondak et al.'s 2.41).
campaigns.volunteer.fix: Give the volunteer choice the person's own free time, interest in the race and agreement with the platform, then calibrate the weight.

staff.follow-through.why: A staffer's follow-through ran 17 times in Jerry City, Ohio's played year and 438 times in New Britain, Connecticut's, where every staffer saw every case through: the work's quality always clears staffCaseFollowThrough, so personality turns none and the study's odds (Barrick and Mount 1991, r .22, 2.44 between the thirds) cannot be reached. The general weight of 1 stands.
staff.follow-through.fix: Let the case's difficulty vary against the staffer's quality, then calibrate (traits-integrity-cases-vary).

staff.hire.why: An official's case varies only with the office's budget, so the willing and unwilling thirds split at lopsided odds whatever the weight (net 20 in Jerry City, Ohio at the general weight). The weight is set from Kardaslar et al. 2026 (odds ratio 1.74 between thirds) over the lean gap between thirds, 0.65.
staff.hire.fix: A case that reads the office's workload (traits-integrity-cases-vary).

staff.dismiss.why: No study gives the odds of dismissing an absent aide by trait; the decision has no weight row of its own and reads the general weight of 1.
staff.dismiss.fix: Add a weight row when a study gives a size.

constituent-cases.bring-case.why: Most residents out of work weigh a case at the same severity (no savings left), so where caseEffort falls in that pile temperament alone sorts them, and the thirds split at lopsided odds whatever the weight (net 44 in Jerry City, Ohio at the general weight). The weight is set from Mondak et al. 2010 (odds ratio 1.68 between thirds) over the lean gap between thirds, 0.51.
constituent-cases.bring-case.fix: Cases that vary, so a problem's own weight spreads the pile (traits-integrity-cases-vary).

appointments.weigh.why: Runs only when an appointer fills a seat that fell vacant between elections (src/core2/appointments.ts); neither drawn year had one.
appointments.weigh.fix: None needed; rare by nature (traits-decisions-never-run measures it in a year that holds a vacancy).
